newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian leading shares rise, LUKoil sets record.
newsitem.headline: Russian leading shares rise, LUKoil sets record.

text.p: Leading Russian shares steamed ahead to new records in early morning Thursday trade on active local and Western buying, traders said, seeing the market strong to closing.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index inched up to a record 534.29 at the opening open from Wednesday's 533.86 close, the second consecutive record finish.
Many leading shares showed gains of over five percent.
Oil company LUKoil climbed to $26.85 at 0855 GMT, off a $27.10 record set earlier in the morning, but up from Wednesday's $24.90 close. National power company UES rose to $0.4465 from $0.4390.
Regional utility Sverdlovenergo rose to $0.990 from $0.910.
Alfa Capital deputy sales director Alexei Genkin said Russian investors were still making most of the buys.
"I think Russian demand will support the market," he said. "I don't see any major falling back."
A Western trader also predicted support would not fade during the day and said Western investors had begun buying.

"We had a lot of local interest over last couple of days," the trader said. "Western fund managers were hoping for prices to come off in August but when they saw it was not happening they piled in too."
